name: Montreal
tagline: North America's most European-feeling city, French colonial streets and a mountain-park summit backed by a food scene built for eating well.
highlight: Standing beneath Notre-Dame Basilica's deep blue, gold-starred ceiling, one of the most ornate church interiors anywhere on the continent.
shortDescription: North America's most European-feeling city, home to French colonial Old Montreal, Notre-Dame Basilica and a food scene built for eating well.
metaDescription: A Montreal travel guide: Notre-Dame Basilica, Old Montreal, Mount Royal Park, Jean-Talon Market, food and how to plan a visit to Quebec's largest city.
knownFor: Notre-Dame Basilica, Old Montreal, Mount Royal Park
intro: Montreal is North America's most European-feeling city, French colonial architecture and a bilingual street life setting it apart from anywhere else on the continent.
Old Montreal's cobblestone streets anchor the historic core, with Notre-Dame Basilica's astonishing interior among the city's true must-sees.
Above it all sits Mount Royal, the wooded hill that gave the city its name, its summit park offering one of the best skyline views in Canada.

whyVisit.intro: Montreal's case rests on a French colonial character found nowhere else in North America, paired with an outstanding food scene.

points.title: It's North America's most European city
points.text: French language, architecture and café culture set it apart from anywhere else on the continent.

points.title: Notre-Dame Basilica is one of the continent's finest church interiors
points.text: A deep blue, gold-starred ceiling unlike almost anywhere else.

points.title: The food scene is exceptional
points.text: Smoked meat, bagels and a real, serious restaurant culture beyond the classics.

points.title: Mount Royal Park is a real asset
points.text: A genuine wooded escape with skyline views, designed by the same architect behind New York's Central Park.

points.title: It works well paired with Quebec City
points.text: An easy, frequent train ride to the province's even more French-feeling capital.

attractionsIntro: Montreal's essential sights are spread between Old Montreal's historic core and the mountain park above it.

attractions.name: Notre-Dame Basilica's interior

image.file: File:Notre-Dame Basilica Interior, Montreal, Canada - Diliff.jpg
image.alt: The interior of Notre-Dame Basilica in Montreal

attractions.text: One of the most ornate church interiors in North America, a deep blue, gold-starred ceiling above intricate wood carving.
attractions.tip: Check for an evening sound and light show, held on select nights.

attractions.name: Old Montreal's cobblestone streets
attractions.text: A well-preserved 17th- and 18th-century quarter, stone buildings and narrow lanes lending real French colonial atmosphere.
attractions.tip: Wander without a fixed route — the neighbourhood rewards getting a little lost.

attractions.name: Mount Royal Lookout

image.file: File:Mount Royal Lookout, Mount Royal Park, Montreal, Quebec (30068343005).jpg
image.alt: The view from Mount Royal Lookout in Montreal

attractions.text: The city's best skyline view, from a park designed by Frederick Law Olmsted, the same architect behind Central Park.
attractions.tip: A rewarding walk or drive up, with a second, quieter lookout further along the summit.

attractions.name: Jean-Talon Market
attractions.text: One of North America's largest public markets, stalls piled with Quebec produce, cheese and prepared foods.
attractions.tip: Combine with a wander through the neighbouring Little Italy district.

attractions.name: Notre-Dame-de-Bon-Secours Chapel
attractions.text: Known as the Sailors' Church, one of the city's oldest, with a rooftop offering harbour views.
attractions.tip: Climb the tower for a view over the Old Port that most visitors miss.

attractions.name: The Old Port

image.file: File:Old Port in Old Montreal. - Le Vieux-Port dans le Vieux-Montréal - panoramio.jpg

attractions.text: A lively waterfront promenade, once a working harbour, now home to parks, bike paths and river cruises.
attractions.tip: A nice spot for an evening walk once the day's heat has eased.

attractions.name: Montreal's downtown skyline
attractions.text: A striking mix of modern towers and historic spires, best appreciated from Mount Royal or the river.
attractions.tip: A river cruise offers a completely different angle on the skyline than the standard viewpoints.

thingsToDoIntro: Montreal rewards splitting time between Old Montreal's history and the city's real food and market culture.

thingsToDo.title: Tour Notre-Dame Basilica's ornate interior

image.file: File:Basílica de Notre-Dame, Montreal, Canadá, 2017-08-12, DD 22-24 HDR.jpg
image.alt: Touring Notre-Dame Basilica's interior in Montreal

thingsToDo.text: An essential Montreal experience, taking in one of the most ornate church interiors in North America.
thingsToDo.tip: Book the AURA light show for an evening visit that shows the basilica in a completely different light.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Old Montreal by horse-drawn carriage

image.alt: A horse-drawn carriage in Old Montreal

thingsToDo.text: A charming, old-fashioned way to see the historic quarter, though walking works just as well.
thingsToDo.tip: Agree the price and route ahead if you do choose a carriage ride.

thingsToDo.title: Hike or picnic in Mount Royal Park

image.alt: The view from Mount Royal Park in Montreal

thingsToDo.text: An essential green escape, trails and picnic spots throughout the park that gave the city its name.
thingsToDo.tip: Visit at golden hour for the best light over the skyline from the lookout.

thingsToDo.title: Sample fresh produce at Jean-Talon Market

image.alt: Fresh produce at Jean-Talon Market in Montreal

thingsToDo.text: A delicious way to spend a morning, sampling Quebec cheese, maple products and seasonal produce.
thingsToDo.tip: Arrive hungry — the market's prepared food stalls are worth the trip alone.

thingsToDo.title: Stroll the Old Port waterfront

image.file: File:Overview of Vieux Montreal Old Port (8390970405).jpg
image.alt: The Old Port waterfront in Montreal

thingsToDo.text: A relaxed way to spend an afternoon, cycling or walking the promenade along the St Lawrence River.
thingsToDo.tip: Rent a bike here to cover more of the waterfront path than walking alone.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Montreal's Underground City
thingsToDo.text: A practical Montreal institution, a vast network of tunnels connecting shops, metro stations and offices below downtown.
thingsToDo.tip: A smart way to get around on a cold winter day without going outside.

foodIntro: Montreal's food stands apart from the rest of Canada, with its own distinct Quebec specialities.

foods.name: Montreal-style bagels
foods.text: Distinct from New York bagels, smaller, sweeter and wood-fired, a real point of local pride.
foods.whereToTry: Bagel bakeries throughout Montreal, especially the city's oldest ones.

foods.name: Smoked meat sandwich

image.file: File:Smoked Meat Sandwich @ Schwartz's Deli @ Le Plateau @ Montréal (30506717566).jpg
image.alt: A smoked meat sandwich, a Montreal specialty

foods.text: A Montreal institution, brisket cured and smoked in-house, piled high on rye bread.
foods.whereToTry: Schwartz's Deli, the dish's most famous and historic source.

foods.name: Poutine

image.alt: Poutine, Canada's fries, cheese curds and gravy dish

foods.text: Born in rural Quebec, and Montreal is one of the best places to try it properly.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants and late-night diners throughout the city.

foods.name: Maple products

image.alt: Maple sap, the source of Quebec's maple syrup

foods.text: A real point of pride, Quebec producing most of the world's maple syrup supply.
foods.whereToTry: Markets and specialty shops throughout the city.

foods.name: Tourtière (meat pie)
foods.text: A traditional Quebec comfort food, a spiced meat pie especially popular around the winter holidays.

foods.name: Quebec cheese
foods.text: An underrated part of the province's food scene, with a real artisanal cheese-making tradition.
foods.whereToTry: Jean-Talon Market and specialty cheese shops throughout the city.

accommodation.intro: Montreal offers accommodation for every budget, with Old Montreal commanding the highest prices.

areas.name: Old Montreal
areas.bestFor: Being immersed in the city's historic atmosphere
areas.text: The most atmospheric, though also the priciest, part of the city to stay.

areas.name: The Plateau or Mile End
areas.text: Close to the city's best bagel shops and a short metro ride from downtown.

gettingThere.intro: Montreal is well connected by air and by Via Rail's Central Canada corridor.

options.text: Available from across North America and Europe.
options.detail: Montréal-Trudeau Airport sits about 30 minutes from downtown.

options.mode: Train from Toronto or Quebec City
options.text: Frequent and comfortable, no car needed.
options.detail: About 4.5 hours from Toronto, or three hours from Quebec City.

options.mode: Bus or drive from Toronto or Quebec City
options.text: A budget-friendly alternative to the train.
options.detail: Similar journey times to rail, with more frequent departures.

gettingAround.intro: Montreal's extensive metro covers the city well, with Old Montreal easily walkable once you're there.

options.text: Fast, frequent and easy to use across the city.
options.detail: Four lines cover downtown, Old Montreal and the surrounding neighbourhoods.

options.text: The best way to explore Old Montreal itself.
options.detail: The historic core is compact and best experienced walking.

options.text: A pleasant way to cover more ground, especially along the Old Port.
options.detail: Stations are widely available throughout the city in warmer months.

bestTime.headline: June to September for warm weather and festival season
bestTime.summary: Montreal is known for a packed summer festival calendar, alongside a cold, snowy winter.

seasons.text: Warm and lively, with major festivals filling the calendar almost every weekend.
Comfortable temperatures with excellent fall colour on Mount Royal.
Cold and snowy, though the Underground City and a lively indoor scene make it workable.
A mild shoulder season, with maple syrup season in nearby sugar shacks.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly — Montreal works as a year-round city break, weather permitting.

itinerary.intro: Built around Old Montreal, Mount Royal Park and the city's food scene.

days.title: Old Montreal
days.afternoon: Wander Old Montreal's cobblestone streets and the Old Port.

days.title: Mount Royal and the markets
days.summary: A day of parks and food.
days.afternoon: Hike or picnic in Mount Royal Park.
days.evening: A smoked meat sandwich at Schwartz's Deli.

days.title: The Plateau and Mile End
days.summary: A slower day exploring local neighbourhoods.
days.afternoon: Explore the Plateau's street art and boutiques.
days.evening: A final dinner reflecting the city's food scene.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Montreal visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book Notre-Dame Basilica's AURA light show ahead for an evening visit.
Learn a few basic French phrases — it's appreciated, even if English is widely understood.
Try both a smoked meat sandwich and a Montreal bagel — they're different institutions.
Use the Underground City in winter to avoid the cold between indoor stops.
Check the festival calendar — summer weekends often have a major event underway.
Combine Montreal with Quebec City for an easy, frequent train connection.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Montreal?
faq.a: Three days covers Old Montreal, Mount Royal Park and the city's food scene comfortably.

faq.q: Do you need to speak French in Montreal?
faq.a: No, not — English is widely understood, though French is the primary language and a few phrases are appreciated.

faq.q: Is Montreal worth visiting compared to Quebec City?
faq.a: Yes — they offer quite different experiences, with Montreal's bigger-city energy complementing Quebec City's more compact colonial charm.
Its French colonial architecture, Notre-Dame Basilica, and a food scene including smoked meat sandwiches and Montreal-style bagels.
Yes, very — temperatures regularly drop well below freezing, though the Underground City makes it manageable.

faq.q: Can you combine Montreal with Quebec City?
faq.a: Yes, easily — a frequent train connects the two in about three hours.
